title: Simple harmonic motion: definition and graphs; Mass–spring and pendulum
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: O01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; O01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; O01-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; O02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: O01-1#N.10a, O01-uk1#N.6, O02-1#N.7b, O01-1#N.11, O02-1#N.8b.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amplitude
items.clue: Maximum displacement of an oscillating object.

items.label: Restoring force
items.clue: Always points back to equilibrium, opposite to the displacement.

items.label: Antiphase
items.clue: Relation between two oscillators of equal T that are π rad, half a cycle, apart.

items.label: Pendulum
items.clue: Its period is longer with a longer string and is unchanged by the mass of the bob.

questions.stem: An object in SHM has a maximum speed v_max and a maximum acceleration of magnitude a_max. Which expression gives the period T of the motion?

options.text: T = 4v_max/a_max
T = v_max/a_max
T = 2πv_max/a_max
T = a_max/(2πv_max)

questions.stem: An object in SHM is released from rest at x = +0.060 m at time t = 0 and oscillates about x = 0 with a period of 1.2 s. What is the object's position at t = 0.20 s?
A pendulum has a period of about 1.5 s and is timed with a hand-held stopwatch. Which method gives the most precise value of the period?

options.text: Time one oscillation from release; repeat 10 times and take the mean.
Time 20 oscillations from a fiducial marker at equilibrium; divide by 20.
Time 20 oscillations from the end of the swing, where the bob is momentarily at rest; divide by 20.
Time half an oscillation and double it.

questions.explanation: The reaction-time error is shared over 20 periods, and the bob moves fastest at equilibrium, so the instant it passes the marker is sharp.

questions.stem: A pendulum bob swings to and fro in a small arc. At the lowest point of its swing, what are its acceleration along its path and its speed?

options.text: Acceleration along the path greatest; speed zero.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed greatest.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed also zero.
Acceleration along the path greatest; speed greatest.

questions.explanation: The lowest point is equilibrium: the restoring force along the path is zero there. The bob sped up all the way down and starts to slow on the way up, so its speed is greatest here.

questions.stem: A pendulum clock keeps correct time at sea level. It is taken to the top of a high mountain, where g is slightly smaller. The length of its pendulum does not change. What happens to the clock?

options.text: It runs fast, as the weaker pull lets the bob swing more freely.
It keeps correct time, as the mass of the bob is unchanged.
It runs slow, as each swing takes slightly longer.
It keeps correct time, as the amplitude of the swing stays small.

questions.explanation: A pendulum's period depends on its length and on g; it is longer where g is smaller. Each tick takes longer, so the clock loses time.
